FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE July 1st, 2026 Todd Achilles Celebrates One Year of Building Idaho's Most Successful Independent Senate Campaign BOISE, Idaho — One year after launching his campaign for the United States Senate, independent candidate Todd Achilles is marking a milestone that reflects growing dissatisfaction with the two-party system and increasing support for independent leadership in Idaho. Over the past year, the Achilles campaign has grown into one of the largest grassroots independent efforts in Idaho politics. The campaign reports raising more money than any previous independent candidate for the U.S. Senate in Idaho and building a statewide network of more than 1,500 volunteers. "One year ago, we set out to prove that Idaho voters deserve a real choice," Achilles said. "Today, we've built a movement powered by volunteers, small-dollar supporters, and people who are tired of a political system that rewards partisan loyalty over public service." Achilles said the campaign's growth comes at a time when many voters are expressing frustration with a political system dominated by the Republican and Democratic parties. The new Supreme Court decision, N ational R epublican Senatorial Committee v. FEC, allows political parties to receive unlimited funds and coordinate the distribution of those funds with donors. This means that anyone can now donate any amount of money to a party and specify which candidate they want it to go to. In other words, contribution limits are now a thing of the past - as long as you’re part of a party. Independents do not have established party fundraising networks, national campaign organizations, or coordinated spending by party committees. They must build campaign infrastructure from the ground up while overcoming restrictive ballot access rules, limited institutional support, and political rules that often favor the two major parties. "The system is increasingly designed to benefit those with access to major donors and party machines, while keeping competition out of the political market" Achilles said. "Too often, voters feel like they come in second at best to political insiders and special interests. Our campaign is proving that Idahoans are ready to build something different." The campaign also criticized the escalating role of outside political spending in Senate races, arguing that national party organizations continue to pour millions of dollars into campaigns while encouraging candidates to focus on fundraising rather than actually engaging with voters. "More campaign money from Washington will never solve Idaho's problems," Achilles said. "Representation comes from listening to the people you serve, not the organizations financing your campaign."

During the past year, Achilles has traveled throughout Idaho, meeting with voters in communities large and small, holding town halls, attending local events, and discussing issues ranging from the cost of living and government accountability to protecting public lands and strengthening rural communities. With four months remaining before Election Day, the campaign said it will continue expanding its volunteer network, increasing voter outreach, and building an independent coalition focused on representing Idaho rather than political parties. ABOUT TODD ACHILLES Todd Achilles, 58, is an Army veteran, former state legislator, public policy professor, and business executive. He grew up on a family farm, served as a U.S. Army tank commander and armor officer, spent over 20 years in senior leadership roles at T-Mobile, Hewlett-Packard, and several technology startups, and served in the Idaho House of Representatives before resigning in July 2025 to launch his U.S. Senate campaign. He lives in Boise with his family. For media inquiries Grace Johnson 208-495-4366 press@achillesforidaho.com www.achillesforidaho.com
